title: Stable vertices and the core of a matching do not depend on the reduction process
source_title: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled proposition, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Short chord and reduction process
standard_prerequisites.statement: A chord is short when it has no vertex strictly between its endpoints; a reduction process removes short chords one after another and pushes the remaining vertices together.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the process whose results the proposition shows to be independent of the choices made.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stable vertex and core
standard_prerequisites.statement: A vertex is stable when it is not removed by any reduction process, and the core of a matching is the matching induced on the stable vertices.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two objects the proposition proves well defined.

core_obligations: Take two reduction processes of the same matching, with removed chords e_1,...,e_k and e'_1,...,e'_k', and argue about the first index l_0 at which the two lists differ (source lines 851-852).

Show that the chords removed earlier by one process are removed earlier by the other as well, so that the chord e_{l_0} is short before it is removed in both processes, and that removing the remaining chords is still a valid reduction (source lines 851-852).
Conclude that the two processes remove the same set of chords, hence that the stable vertices and the core are independent of the process (source line 852).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up two reduction processes and compare their removal lists.
Take the first deviation, show the deviating chord is short in both processes and derive a contradiction.
Conclude equality of the removed sets, hence well-definedness of the stable vertices and the core.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 846-849: given a matching, its stable vertices and its core are well defined. The proof (source lines 850-853) is an exchange argument on two reduction processes run on the same matching: one compares the two lists of removed chords, takes the first position at which they differ, and uses the fact that the deviating chord had to become short before being removed in both processes to derive a contradiction, which forces the two lists to remove the same chords. The statement is a well-definedness claim for two constructions and records neither the process comparison nor the minimal-deviation argument, and the argument has to be carried through the vertex renumbering that each removal performs.
